newsitem.title: JORDAN: Iraq and Jordan discuss oil-for-food trade.
newsitem.headline: Iraq and Jordan discuss oil-for-food trade.

text.p: Iraq's Minister of Trade Mohammed Mehdi Saleh met Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti on Monday to discuss Jordanian efforts to supply Baghdad with food and medicine under its U.N. food-for-oil deal.
"The meeting was concentrated on discussing the means by which we can develop our economic and trade relationship," Saleh told reporters after his talks with Kabariti.
He said the two men also discussed plans for a meeting of economic ministers "through which our bilateral relationship of economy and trade will be enlarged hopefully in the future."

Jordan, which has distanced itself politically from its neighbour and largest trading partner, is still keen to capitalise on an easing of the six-year sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Jordanian vegetable oil, pharmaceutical and detergent producers are eager to increase their sales to Baghdad, and Jordan hopes that increased use of its only port, at Aqaba on the Red Sea, will also breathe life into its economy.

"We welcome the participation of Jordanian companies and traders to export commodities and food," Saleh said. "We have discussed how to enlarge our use of Aqaba in importing our commodities through the (oil-for-food deal) as well as our trade for different commodities," he said.

Saleh told Jordan's Chamber of Industry on Sunday that Jordanians had a competitive advantage in a range of industries, including vegetable oils and drugs, under the U.N. deal that allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil every six months to buy humanitarian needs.

He also said Iraq would give Jordanian industrialists who had continued to supply Iraq with goods exempted by sanctions "preference provided their prices were comparable" to other international bidders.
He said wheat imports would consume the largest share of the oil-for food deals, followed by rice, sugar, vegetable oils detergents and soaps.
